description:
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:152-156 — SctVerifier<V: SignatureVerifier> wraps a generic V instead of hardcoding ECDSA or RSA implementations. Algorithm dispatch is delegated to pkix-path's SignatureVerifier trait via tls_alg_to_x509_oid (line 106).

This is exactly what workspace non-negotiable #3 requires for pkix-path ('SignatureVerifier is the only place algorithm-specific code lives in pkix-path'). pkix-ct extends the same pattern: no signature crate or key parsing crate is pulled in by pkix-ct itself; the caller's SignatureVerifier handles ECDSA/RSA/anything-else.

Concrete consequences:
- pkix-ct works with any backend the caller plugs in (pkix-path::DefaultVerifier, a custom ring-based one, a custom FIPS-validated one, a PQ-ready one).
- pkix-ct does not pull in p256/p384/rsa as direct deps; those live in pkix-path's optional features.
- Adding a new algorithm to pkix-ct (e.g., the EdDSA-Ed25519 combo that future CT logs might use) is a one-line addition to tls_alg_to_x509_oid — no new dep in pkix-ct itself.

A future contributor might suggest 'simplify by hardcoding ECDSA-P256-SHA256 since that's all CT logs use today' — would break the abstraction and lock pkix-ct to one algorithm. The trait-based design is the right call. Defend it.
title: SignatureVerifier dispatch keeps algorithm code out of pkix-ct, in line with workspace non-negotiable #3
